title: Kyūshū Loop in 8 Days — Fukuoka, Yufuin, Beppu, Takachiho, Kumamoto
subtitle: In and out of Fukuoka, with Yufuin, Beppu, Kumamoto and a Takachiho day tour, then back to Fukuoka and Itoshima
summary: Eight days around Kyūshū: Fukuoka, Yufuin, the Beppu hot springs, Kumamoto and a Takachiho day tour, then back to Fukuoka for a trip out to Itoshima. Takachiho is written as a joined day tour, with no agency named. On day 5 (the day tour) and day 7 (Itoshima), travel will take more than a third of the day — that is simply the distance. Karatsu, Yūtoku Inari and Takeo sit in the alternates.
destination: Japan: Fukuoka, Yufuin, Beppu, Kumamoto, Takachiho

Opening hours and closing days of Tōchō-ji, Ōhori Park, Yunotsubo Street, Lake Kinrin, Beppu Tower, Myōban Jigoku, Katō Shrine, the Kamitori and Shimotori arcades, Takachiho Shrine, Amano Iwato Shrine, Ama no Yasugawara, the Luffy statue, Sakurai Futamigaura, Sakurai Shrine and Nanzō-in.
Bus times, fares and last bus from Yufuin to Beppu; the itinerary, meeting point and price of the Takachiho day tour.
Current highway bus times from Kumamoto Station to Takachiho.
Changes and trade-offs
The travelogue is an 11-day trip that arrives at Hakata by cruise ship from Busan; the Busan and cruise parts are not used, and this becomes a Kyūshū loop in and out of Fukuoka Airport.

The travelogue has no Kumamoto section (the 2023 Kyūshū travelogue does), so this adds that travelogue's Katō Shrine, Kamitori and Shimotori and the Luffy statue in Kumamoto, ordered as Beppu → Kumamoto → Takachiho → Fukuoka around the loop.
In the travelogue Takachiho is a day tour from Fukuoka; this version departs from Kumamoto (written, by rule, as joining a day tour with no operator named).
Karatsu, Yūtoku Inari, Takeo Onsen, Shimonoseki and Sasebo from the travelogue are not on the loop; Karatsu, Yūtoku Inari and Takeo are kept as alternates.
This version deliberately avoids spots already used by the Kita-Kyūshū and Kumamoto–Aso templates (Mojikō, Dazaifu, Yanagawa, Kumamoto Castle, Aso, Suizenji and others).
On day 5 (the day tour) and day 7 (Itoshima), the share of travel time goes above the usual 30%; that is simply the distance.
From the travelogue

Lodging is written by area only: the travelogue stayed at Toyoko Inn Hakata-guchi Ekimae, Toyoko Inn Ōita Ekimae and APA Fukuoka Watanabe-dōri; for Beppu and Kumamoto the author recommends nothing, so only the area around the station is written.
Route
A Kyūshū loop in and out of Fukuoka: Fukuoka → Yufuin → Beppu → Kumamoto → Takachiho (day tour) → Fukuoka.
Nights: Fukuoka 1, Beppu 2, Kumamoto 2, Fukuoka 2.
Entry and internet
Before you leave, register for immigration and customs on Visit Japan Web: https://www.vjw.digital.go.jp/main/#/vjwpco001
For internet, use a physical SIM card or an eSIM.
Airport to the city

The international terminal at Fukuoka Airport has no subway station: first take the free shuttle bus, about 10 minutes, to the domestic terminal, then the Kūkō Line subway to Hakata Station, about 5 minutes and ¥260, transit IC cards accepted; with baggage claim and walking, allow a cautious 30–40 minutes.
The travelogue says the shuttle runs every 5–10 minutes, and from the subway station back to the international departure hall you should add about 30 minutes.
Transport passes
This route uses many limited expresses (Hakata → Yufuin, Beppu → Kumamoto), so before you go compare single tickets with a JR Kyushu rail pass: https://www.jrkyushu.co.jp/chinese/

Reminder from the 2024 travelogue: if you reserve seats online with a JR pass, you must show the same credit card when exchanging; the pass does not cover the San'yō Shinkansen and some Shinkansen trains, so check at the Shinkansen gates (travelogue, 2024 data).
Yufuin no Mori has all seats reserved; the unreserved seats on the Kyushu Odan limited express are in car 2.
At unstaffed small stations, get off from the first car and show your pass directly; at an unstaffed JR station, do not drop the pass into the ticket collection box on exit (travelogue).
Yufuin to Beppu
Kamenoi Bus runs the ‘Kankō Kaisoku Yufurin’ and route 36 between Yufuin Station and Beppu Station; check the Kamenoi Bus website for the time and fare, or take JR with a change at Ōita.
Beppu Jigoku is open about 8:00–17:00 all year; Myōban Jigoku, planned for the afternoon, must be left by 17:00 at the latest.
Takachiho day tour

Several agencies run this day tour (from both Kumamoto and Fukuoka, covering Takachiho Shrine, Takachiho Gorge, Amano Iwato Shrine and Ama no Yasugawara); before you go compare itineraries, meeting points and whether lunch is included.

To go by public transport on your own: take the highway bus ‘Takachiho-gō’ from in front of Kumamoto Station to Takachiho Bus Center, about ¥2,700 one way (old data compiled online — check times and fare before you go); there are no buses to Amano Iwato Shrine and Ama no Yasugawara on weekdays, so take a taxi, while weekends and peak season have a loop bus.

Boats on Takachiho Gorge are booked online only: the booking opens 2 weeks before the ride day at 9:00 and closes 2 days before at 9:00, and sells out quickly in peak season. If you want a boat, ask the agency first whether it can fit your time.
Around Kumamoto

The city mostly runs on trams and buses. The 2024 travelogue update says several bus operators in Kumamoto Prefecture and Kumamoto Electric Railway no longer take Suica and other transit IC cards, so carry yen in cash and check the current situation first.
Other
Carry plenty of yen in cash: some small shops, buses and small stations do not take cards.
On days 6 and 8 you use the hotel's luggage storage; hotels such as Toyoko Inn will usually hold bags at the desk.
The lockers at Yufuin Station have few spaces for suitcases; the travelogue advises going straight there on arrival.
Adjust the airport time on the last day to your actual flight.
About the route: this template focuses on moving around Kyūshū; the Fukuoka spots on days 1, 7 and 8 do not repeat the Kita-Kyūshū (Mojikō, Dazaifu, Yanagawa) or Kumamoto–Aso templates.

notes.title: Trip overview: how the 8 days run
paragraphs: In and out of Fukuoka, with a loop around Kyushu: Fukuoka, Yufuin, Beppu, Kumamoto and Takachiho, then back to Fukuoka and a day out to Itoshima. You change bases four times: one night in Fukuoka, two in Beppu, two in Kumamoto and two back in Fukuoka. JR limited expresses and the Kyushu Shinkansen carry most of the travel, and Takachiho is done as a day tour.
Day 1: land in the morning, take the subway to Hakata for lunch and to leave your bags, visit {@d1-03} in the afternoon, then walk around the lake at {@d1-04}, and have dinner in Tenjin.
Day 2: the Yufuin no Mori limited express from Hakata in the morning, lunch in Yufuin, then {@d2-02} and Lake Kinrin, a bus to Beppu in the evening, and the night view from {@d2-04}.
Day 3: a full day of the Beppu hells, starting with {@d3-01} and Kamado Jigoku, hell curry for lunch, {@d3-04} in the afternoon, then Myoban Jigoku, and the bus back to Beppu Station at dusk.
Day 4: the early Kyushu Odan limited express from Beppu through Aso to Kumamoto, then {@d4-02} after lunch for the view of Kumamoto Castle from behind, and {@d4-03}, with dinner in Shimotori.
Day 5: a full day tour to Takachiho for {@d5-02} and its wedded cedars and a walk through {@d5-04}, then Amano Iwato Shrine and Ama no Yasugawara, and back to Kumamoto at night.
Day 6: the {@d6-01} in front of the prefectural office in the morning, the Kyushu Shinkansen back to Hakata, and a bus to {@d6-03} in the afternoon to see the life-size Gundam.
Day 7: out to Itoshima for {@d7-01} and Sakurai Shrine, back to Hakata after lunch, and anime goods and toy shops around Tenjin in the evening.
Day 8: check out, then JR Sasaguri Line to {@d8-01} for the reclining Buddha, lunch in Hakata, collect your bags and take the subway and the shuttle bus to the airport.

Where to sleep: the first night near Hakata Station, two nights near Beppu Station, two nights near Kumamoto Station, and the last two nights back near Hakata Station; on days 6 and 8 you leave your bags at the hotel.

Getting around: Hakata to Yufuin is the Yufuin no Mori, all reserved seats; Yufuin to Beppu is the Kamenoi bus, or JR with a change at Oita; Beppu to Kumamoto is the Kyushu Odan limited express; Kumamoto to Hakata is the Kyushu Shinkansen; Takachiho is a day tour, about 2.5 hours each way; Itoshima takes JR and a bus from Hakata, about 80 to 90 minutes each way; since you ride a lot of limited expresses, compare single tickets with the JR Kyushu rail pass. On day 5 (the day tour) and day 7 (Itoshima) more than a third of the time goes on transit, which is simply the distance. Buses and trams in Kumamoto may not take transport IC cards, so carry yen in cash. Check the latest timetables before you go.

Who it suits: anyone who wants the big Kyushu sights in one trip and accepts long transfers for the hot springs, the gorge and the shrines. You move or ride for hours most days, so wear comfortable shoes and pack light; at Nanzo-in, wear long trousers and cover your shoulders.

leg.note: From the Nishi Hongū walk about 15 minutes to Ama no Yasugawara; there are ice cream shops on the way back

events.notes: Check opening hours before you go

closingLeg.note: Walk back to the hotel from Kumamoto Station

events.title: Lunch: around Hakata Station

place.name: Hakata
place.address: 福岡県福岡市博多区, 博多駅中央街

leg.note: Go back to the hotel for your bags and on to Kumamoto Station, about 30 minutes; the Kyushu Shinkansen from Kumamoto to Hakata takes about 38 minutes, and an unreserved seat costs about ¥5,310 (compiled by a private site — check the JR website)

events.title: LaLaport Fukuoka (ららぽーと福岡): the life-size νGundam
events.notes: 10:00–21:00 (the mall's hours as given on Wikipedia); check each shop's hours before you go

leg.note: First go back to the hotel to leave your bags (about 10 minutes on foot), then take a Nishitetsu bus from Hakata Bus Terminal to ‘LaLaport Fukuoka’, about 20 minutes; the stop is right at the mall

leg.note: Take a Nishitetsu bus back to Hakata, about 20 minutes

closingLeg.note: Walk back to the hotel from dinner

events.title: Sakurai Futamigaura and the Wedded Rocks (桜井二見ヶ浦)

place.name: Sakurai Futamigaura
place.address: 〒819-1304, 福岡県糸島市, 志摩桜井

events.notes: Open all day; the sea torii and the Wedded Rocks look different with the weather and tide

leg.note: Leave around 8:15: JR from Hakata to Kyudai-Gakkentoshi Station takes about 35–40 minutes, then a bus (the Nishinoura line in the travelogue) takes about 30 minutes and costs ¥730 (travelogue, 2024 data; check times before you go)

leg.note: About 10 minutes on foot from behind the Wedded Rocks (the travelogue says you can go farther back)

events.title: Lunch: around Sakurai Futamigaura

place.address: 〒819-1304, 福岡県糸島市, 志摩桜井

leg.note: Bus and JR back to Hakata take about 80–90 minutes, then the subway to Tenjin about 5 minutes; Itoshima is far, so this day has a higher share of travel time

events.title: Nanzō-in (南蔵院): the reclining Buddha
events.notes: Check opening hours before you go; the travelogue says sleeveless tops and shorts that bare the midriff or shoulders, playing music, dancing and photography in some areas are not allowed

leg.note: After checking out, leave your bags at the hotel desk; from Hakata Station take the JR Sasaguri Line to Nanzōin-mae Station, about 30–35 minutes; from the exit go past Kōjin Chaya and cross the road to the entrance (travelogue)

events.title: Depart from Fukuoka Airport (Fukuoka Kūkō)

leg.note: Go back to the hotel for your bags (about 5 minutes on foot); the Kūkō Line subway from Hakata to the domestic terminal takes about 5 minutes, then the free shuttle bus to the international terminal about 10 minutes; the travelogue advises reaching the departure hall with 30 extra minutes; adjust to your actual flight
